rules._comment: Interface v0.17–v0.18, The Player's Words: the rules modal's text, written for the player, in place of the AI guests' primer (Technical Design's block 2, which is unchanged). One entry per section, in the order a player learns the evening: its `title`, then its paragraphs. A paragraph is a string, or a list of parts joined with a space. A part is a string; or {"when": <condition>, "text": …} or {"unless": <condition>, "text": …}, shown only then; or {"clauses": […], "and": …, "end": …}, a list of clauses joined with commas and a last `and`, leaving out any clause that names a value the run doesn't have. The conditions: `plotReward` (the run's plot_reward flag) and `chanceEachRound` (a round of mingling has at least as many turns as there are living guests). The {placeholders} are the game's values, sent with the player's sheet (Technical Design v0.52, Player Interface, The screen, "The game's values"): {start}, {income}, {payroll}, {vote}, {treasury}, {currency} (the plural), {linesPerTurn}, {minglingTurns}, {councilTurns}, {finalCouncilTurns}, {selectionTurns}, {openFloorTurns}, {colloquioCap}. Never a number typed in. Lines that start "1." are a numbered list.

sections.title: The Evening
text: Tonight the city's factions (the Medici, the Pazzi, the Dominicans, and the French Embassy) scheme over who will be elected Gonfaloniere, the head of Florence's government. Only a Medici or a Pazzi may stand.

sections.title: How to Win
text:
The moment the vote is announced, the winner is decided in this order.
1. The Dominicans win if the elected candidate has publicly repented.
2. Otherwise, the French Embassy wins if anyone in the winner's family is on France's payroll, as long as one member of the Embassy still lives.
3. Otherwise, the elected candidate's family, Medici or Pazzi, wins.
A faction needs at least one living member to win. You win if your faction does, even if you died along the way. A candidate who repents changes sides: from then on, they win only if the Dominicans do.

sections.title: Your Errand
text: Your briefing gives you one task of your own tonight, and it comes first.

text.text: Finish it before the last council before midnight and you secretly earn one extra act at midnight: a second kill, guard, or watch, on a different guest. No one else is told.
In this game, finishing it earns no extra act at midnight.

sections.title: The Order of the Evening
text: Three rounds of mingling, each followed by a council of your own faction. Then midnight. Then the Medici and Pazzi each choose a candidate, the candidates give speeches, every faction holds one last council, and the secret ballot ends the evening.

sections.title: Stages and Turns
text: The evening moves in stages, shown in the bar at the top of the screen. The rounds of mingling, the councils, the choosing of candidates, and the open floor after the speeches are made of turns; midnight and the ballot are single choices.
A turn is {linesPerTurn} lines spoken across the whole house, shared among every conversation at once.

clauses: A round of mingling lasts {minglingTurns} turns
the open floor after the speeches {openFloorTurns}

text: In a group or a council, you say one thing each turn. Type whenever you like, and your words are said at the next pause in your conversation. Pass gives up your line for the turn. If someone speaks to you directly, the game waits for your answer, and answering doesn't use up your line.
In a secret conversation, the two of you take turns, and the game waits for you each time. It lasts {colloquioCap} lines at most, and either of you can end it sooner; the other then gets a last word.
Moving. At the end of every turn, one guest gets a chance to move, in an order drawn fresh at the start of each round of mingling.

text.text: So you get at least one chance each round.
A round has fewer turns than there are guests, so not everyone gets a chance every round.

text: When yours comes, you can stay, join another guest's group, or start a secret conversation with any guest. You move toward a person, not to a place. If your chance comes while you're in a secret conversation, you stay where you are and the chance is lost. The line above the message box says when yours is next.

sections.title: Conversations
text: Guests talk in groups of two to four, or two slip away into a secret conversation (a Colloquio), which no one else can join or hear. Starting one uses your chance to move, and the guest you choose can't refuse.

Il Notaio, the evening's notary, notes who joins, who leaves, and who slips away, and everyone present hears his notes, so slipping away often invites suspicion. Everyone can see who is in which part of the house, but only those in a conversation hear what's said.

When a secret conversation ends, the guest who was invited chooses first, from the groups with room or a secret conversation of their own, which costs them no move. The one who started it goes back to the group they left, or to the smallest group if that one is full or has broken up.

sections.title: Money and Bribes
text: Everyone begins with {start} {currency} and receives {income} more at the start of each round of mingling. Purses are private. A bribe is {currency} handed to the guest you're in a secret conversation with (/bribe); whatever is promised in return is a matter of honor, not law.

sections.title: France's Payroll
text: Any Medici or Pazzi may take a payroll payment of {payroll} {currency} from the French Embassy's treasury (/borrow), which puts them on France's payroll. The treasury starts with {treasury} {currency}; while it's empty, there's no payment to take until one is paid back. Each payment can be paid back before the ballot, {payroll} {currency} at a time (/repay), by the one who took it or by a relative who knows of it; with every payment paid back, they're off the payroll. The payroll is private; only the Embassy keeps the full ledger.

sections.title: Midnight
text: Each living guest secretly chooses one act: to kill, guard, or watch someone. All acts take effect at once, so a guest who dies at midnight still carries out their own act. A guest guarded by two or more survives an attack. A guest watched by two or more can't carry out their kill. You can't guard yourself. Killers are never named. The dead lose their {currency} and their place on France's payroll; nothing is inherited.

sections.title: Candidates and the Vote
text: After midnight, the Medici and the Pazzi each choose one living member as their candidate. Each candidate gives a speech, and then anyone may speak.

During the speeches only, a candidate may publicly repent (/repent). It's permanent. The candidate changes sides: from then on they win only if the Dominicans do, and if they're elected, the Dominicans win.

After one last council, every living guest casts one secret vote for any living guest, and may buy extra votes for that same guest at {vote} {currency} each (/buy). Most votes wins, and Il Notaio names only the winner. If the top guests tie, everyone votes once more among only those guests, with no buying; if that ties too, the winner is drawn by lot.
